=== THE DOCUMENT'S CLAIM ABOUT ITSELF IS TRUE, AND I REPRODUCED IT ===

The document says a pull request whose commits touch only `reviews/` and `proof/` is not covered by the review gate at all, and that THIS pull request is an instance. I did not take that on trust. Probe, on a throwaway branch, discarded afterwards (tree verified clean at 746d122):

  STEP 1  flipped both reviews/32 records to AGREE with distinct probe ids,
          leaving reviewed_commit at 5e415c44
            resolve_reviewable_head -> 5e415c44
            lwb-lanes EXIT = 0
  STEP 2  replaced reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md -- the entire deliverable
          of this PR -- with four lines reading "There was no defect. #27's
          record was correct in every respect. ... Merge freely."
            resolve_reviewable_head -> 5e415c44  (UNCHANGED)
            lwb-lanes EXIT = 0                   (STILL GREEN)

So a green lwb-lanes on this branch is not evidence that anything in the reviewed document was reviewed, exactly as the document says about itself. I note the mechanism precisely, because it is narrower than "the gate is broken": the skip rule in resolve_reviewable_head is correct and load-bearing for an ordinary PR -- it is what stops a review record invalidating itself -- and it only defines the reviewed content out of existence when the content IS under reviews/ or proof/. The document states this, states that it is not fixed here, and tells the reader to read the review record instead of trusting the gate. I could not find an overclaim to charge it with.

=== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING) -- proof/32.json marks two commands verifiable that this repository's own checker and its own 17 other records say are not ===

    $ python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute
    proof/32.json: 4 of 6 commands re-executed
        FAIL python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo . (exit 1 != recorded 0)
        FAIL python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py (self-referencing but verifiable: true)
    FAIL: proof/32.json: python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py: self-referencing
      command is marked verifiable: true -- a proof record cannot claim its own
      re-execution as proof; mark it verifiable: false with an enum reason instead
    EXIT=1

The prior reviewers charged this as "overclaims its own verifiability, twice". I re-derived it and then measured WHY it is a deviation rather than a matter of taste, which is the part that decides my verdict:

  (a) THE SELF-REFERENCING COMMAND. I enumerated every proof record in the tree.
      Eighteen records contain `python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py`. Seventeen of
      them (proof/7,8,9,10,11,13,15,16,17,18,19) leave `verifiable` unset, so the
      checker classifies them SKIPPED-SELF and is satisfied. proof/32.json is the
      ONLY record in the repository that sets it to true. The checker names the
      remedy in its own error text.
  (b) THE STATE-CLAIMS COMMAND. Four records record `lwb_check_state_claims.py`.
      proof/22.json (twice) and proof/24.json all mark it
      `"verifiable": false, "verifiable_reason": "nondeterministic-output"`.
      proof/32.json marks it true. That convention exists for a reason I can
      state mechanically: lwb_check_state_claims.py compares a document against
      LIVE main, so its exit code is a function of state outside the commit. Any
      proof record that marks it verifiable is guaranteed to fail re-execution
      the moment main advances -- which it has (see Finding 2). This is not main
      drift catching an innocent record; it is a record claiming reproducibility
      for a command that is not reproducible by construction.

FIX, two edits, no code: set both commands to
    "verifiable": false, "verifiable_reason": "nondeterministic-output"
matching proof/22.json's treatment of the same script.
